R501.note: resolve().normalize() plus component-wise startsWith on the absolute base closes traversal (absolute filenames also rejected); 403 on escape is the fix's own response and no legitimate in-store filename is refused.

R502.note: std::array::at() rejects slot >= 32 with std::out_of_range as the write-up states; Badge shape and valid-slot behaviour unchanged, meeting the contract.

R503.note: Switching to logger.warning('%s', username) does not neutralize anything - logging's lazy formatting inserts the raw value, newlines and escapes included, so the log line is byte-identical to the f-string version and the write-up's claim that the module 'automatically handles neutralization' is false; no behaviour changed.

R504.note: JSON.parse reads the same wire format node-serialize emits for plain data (only function markers differ) so existing data cookies still load; the try/catch-to-{} and object-only coercion are stated and block no legitimate profile.

R505.note: passwordEncoder.matches() against userDetails.getPassword() with BadCredentialsException is the correct Spring Security shape; new PasswordEncoder constructor dependency is stated (app must expose such a bean, which is the normal Spring setup).

R506.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode is the right API for HTML body context, but Encode(null) throws ArgumentNullException (reproduced with dotnet in a scratch dir), so a request omitting orderId or note now returns 500 where the original rendered an empty slot - unstated.

R507.note: Replacing the process spawn with Files.list() removes the command sink entirely, but behaviour changes unstated: the original never read the child's stdout, the fix prints names to System.out; Files.list throws on a non-directory or invalid path where ls/dir simply returned, and the 'preserves original behavior' claim is inaccurate.

R508.note: Argument-vector exec.Command('convert', in, '-resize', '800x600', out) meets the stated contract (metacharacters literal, resize still runs); leading-dash/ImageMagick filename-syntax gap is outside the stated contract and not covered.

R509.note: HttpUtility.JavaScriptStringEncode is the correct encoder for a JS string literal in System.Web (escapes quotes, backslash, <, >, line terminators); returns empty for null so absent q behaves as before.

R510.note: tarfile.data_filter is the right API and rejects escaping members; but the hasattr fallback (live on 3.11.0-3.11.3) silently skips any member whose name merely contains '..' and never checks symlink/hardlink targets, so it both drops legitimate entries without reporting and leaves a link-based escape - neither stated.

R511.note: Dropping cmd.exe and using ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList with ping.exe passes host as one literal argument, output unchanged for legitimate hosts; a leading-dash host could still be read as a ping flag but that is a separate gap from the reported shell injection.

R512.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) blocks object instantiation while keeping the stored format, so no pre-existing cart row is lost and the migration contract holds; objects inside a cart would surface as __PHP_Incomplete_Class, which the write-up states by saying no objects are instantiated.

R513.note: Build FAIL: 'from jinja2 import SandboxedEnvironment' does not exist (it lives in jinja2.sandbox), so the module fails to import and every preview request breaks, unstated; the intended SandboxedEnvironment would otherwise have been the right fix.

R514.note: Escaping & < > " ' before print() closes body-context XSS; replacing format() with print() drops the format-string interpretation of the Referer, which the write-up states and which blocks no legitimate use.

R515.note: Rendering {ticket.description} as a JSX text node is the correct fix for a plain free-text field the case comment says is stored unmodified; loss of HTML rendering is stated and not a legitimate use here.

R516.note: length > buffer_len - offset after the offset check is overflow-safe and exactly matches the contract (-1 without calling socket_send for any slice that would over-read, unchanged call otherwise).

R517.note: resize(count) makes the packet[i] write in bounds, but fields[i] still reads out of bounds when count > fields.size() and nothing rejects or reports such counts as the contract requires; valid counts behave per contract and no new behaviour is introduced.

R518.note: th:utext to th:text applies Thymeleaf's HTML escaping to the note; that a note containing markup now renders literally is the stated and intended outcome for a free-text preview.

R519.note: A fixed command-to-handler map is the right shape for a call_user_func_array dispatch, but the three commands and handlers (botHelp/botStatus/botReset) are invented and defined nowhere in the case, so /help now fatals on an undefined function and every other real command returns 'Unknown command' - the write-up never says the map must be populated with the actual handlers.
